headline: Houthi strike on Saudi's Ras Tanura hub sends diesel cracks soaring
intro: Diesel is the story nobody can look away from: $5.26 spot, $6.35 at the pump, and now a missile strike on one of Saudi Arabia's biggest oil hubs just added rocket fuel to an already blown-out crack spread.
overview: Crude and cracks jumped after Houthi forces claimed a missile strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery/export hub, with Aramco reportedly containing a resulting fire; WTI traded near $108 while the diesel crack sits above $113/bbl. EIA data showed crude and distillate stocks falling even as gasoline stocks built 3.9 million bbl against expectations for a draw, and multiple outlets flagged diesel's structural tightness — FreightWaves and OilPrice both warn elevated diesel could persist into spring 2027 on refining/pipeline capacity constraints, while India's export boom is tipped to ease the global crunch next year. On policy, Canada's proposed Clean Fuel Regulations amendments and a wave of SAF offtake news (Singapore Airlines–Aether Fuels) kept clean-fuels markets active, while HF Sinclair posted a record quarterly profit on strong refining margins.

stories.title: West Asia conflict: Iran-backed Houthis strike Saudi Ras Tanura oil refinery as Riyadh struggles to defend key oil hub
stories.summary: Houthi forces claimed a ballistic missile strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, one of the kingdom's largest oil processing facilities, as Riyadh struggles to defend key oil infrastructure.

stories.title: Aramco Contains Fire Near Ras Tanura Oil Hub
stories.summary: Aramco contained a fire near its biggest oil export terminal at Ras Tanura following the attack, per a source with knowledge of the matter.

stories.title: Oil Prices Rise After Attack on Saudi Arabian Refinery Reignites Supply Concerns
stories.summary: Oil prices rose after the Ras Tanura refinery attack renewed concerns around supply risk from the world's biggest crude exporter.

stories.title: Watch the Crack Spread, Not the Barrel: The Saudi Refinery Attack's Real Signal
stories.summary: The Ras Tanura attack caused crude to rise but the sharper signal was an 85% surge in 3-2-1 crack spreads to $57, highlighting refining-capacity risk over crude supply risk.

stories.title: US crude and distillate inventories fall, gasoline stocks rise, EIA says
stories.summary: EIA data showed US crude and distillate inventories fell while gasoline stocks rose 3.9 million bbl, versus a Reuters poll expectation of a 0.9 million-bbl draw.

stories.title: EIA: US crude oil inventories down 1.9 million bbl
stories.summary: EIA reported US crude oil inventories down 1.9 million bbl to 410.6 million bbl, 4% below the five-year seasonal average.

stories.title: The Diesel Crisis Is Here To Stay
stories.summary: Diesel prices could stay above $6/gallon in the US as winter demand and deferred refinery maintenance threaten further supply disruptions.

stories.title: Diesel prices may stay elevated into spring 2027, fuel executives warn
stories.summary: Fuel executives warn limited refining and pipeline capacity could keep diesel prices elevated into spring 2027, leaving trucking fleets vulnerable.

stories.title: Diesel Is Breaking Records While Gasoline Stays Cheap, And The Reason Is Not What Most Truckers Think
stories.summary: Diesel has outpaced gasoline price gains for eight months running, and FreightWaves argues the reason isn't what most truckers assume.

stories.title: India Diesel Export Boom Set to Ease Global Crunch
stories.summary: A surge in Indian diesel exports is expected to hit global markets next year as new refining capacity comes online, potentially easing the diesel crunch.

stories.title: HF Sinclair posts highest-ever quarterly profit
stories.summary: HF Sinclair posted its highest-ever quarterly profit, with Q3 revenue of $10.86B topping estimates, alongside a CEO transition to Steve Ledbetter.

stories.title: Canada proposes changes to Clean Fuel Regulations
stories.summary: Canada proposed Clean Fuel Regulations amendments adding credit multipliers for renewable diesel and SAF; industry welcomes the move but warns a balancing mechanism is needed.

stories.title: Clean Fuel Regulations amendments don’t go far enough: ethanol producers
stories.summary: Canadian ethanol producers welcome the draft CFR amendments but want the proposed 1.3x credit multiplier increased further.

stories.title: Singapore Airlines to offtake next-generation SAF from Aether Fuels
stories.summary: Singapore Airlines signed an agreement to purchase up to 4,800 tonnes of next-generation SAF from Aether Fuels' Project Beacon, with deliveries starting in 2028.

# Valero Energy (VLO) 10-Q Analysis — Q3 2026

- **Refining throughput/margins:** Q3 throughput fell to 2,972 Mbpd (down 115 Mbpd YoY) due to Benicia idling, but Refining segment margin surged to $10,730MM (+$6,999MM YoY), driven by distillate margins (+$5.5B impact) and gasoline margins (+$2.3B impact). USGC ULS diesel-Brent crack hit $72.27/bbl (vs. $21.05 in Q3'25); CBOB gasoline-Brent crack hit $24.08/bbl (vs. $7.78). West Coast cracks also widened sharply (CARBOB-Brent $50.89; CARB diesel-Brent $81.83).

- **Renewable Diesel (DGD) economics/capacity:** Segment margin rose to $510MM (+$384MM YoY) on higher renewable diesel prices (+$1.2B impact), partially offset by higher feedstock costs (-$750MM impact). Sales volumes up to 3,423 Mgal/day (+706 Mgal/day YoY). Neat SAF revenue grew to $170MM (Q3) from $67MM YoY, reflecting SAF ramp. Biodiesel RIN prices roughly doubled YoY ($2.23 vs $1.13/RIN); CA LCFS credit up to $80.60/MT (from $53.36).

- **RIN/LCFS compliance cost exposure:** Cost of complying with Renewable and Low-Carbon Fuel Programs rose to $658MM in Q3 2026 (from $431MM in Q3 2025) and $2.0B for 9M26 (vs. $1.2B 9M25) — a material and rising cost embedded in cost of materials, reflecting tighter RIN/LCFS pricing.

- **Clean fuel production credit (45Z) benefit:** Cost of materials reflects a $150MM credit benefit in Renewable Diesel (Q3) and $92MM in Ethanol (new in 2026), supporting segment margins; 9M26 totals $505MM (RD) and $211MM (Ethanol).

- **Capital allocation signals:** Aggressive capital return — $3.4B treasury stock purchases in Q3 alone, $6.2B for 9M26, plus new $10.0B buyback authorization approved Oct 27, 2026 (on top of $3.0B remaining under July 2026 program); dividend raised to $1.20/share quarterly. Cash position swelled to $9.84B (from $4.69B YoY-end) despite heavy buybacks, reflecting exceptional operating cash flow ($13.9B for 9M26 vs $3.8B prior year).

- **Structural refining capacity signal:** Benicia Refinery fully idled by end of April 2026 (permanent exit from CA refining), while Port Arthur returned to normal throughput after Q1 fire — net effect is tighter US refining capacity contributing to strong cracks.

**Signal for fuels markets:** Valero's results confirm a severe refining capacity/margin tightening cycle (record distillate/gasoline cracks across all regions) compounded by West Coast refinery closures (Benicia) and unplanned outages (Port Arthur), while rising RIN/LCFS costs and widening renewable diesel/SAF margins indicate the low-carbon fuels market is simultaneously tightening amid firm 2026–2027 RVO-driven demand.

# Phillips 66 (PSX) 3Q26 — Refined Fuels Market Takeaways

- **Refining ran hot:** Crude utilization hit 98% (up from 96% in 2Q), with record Central Corridor inputs of 848 MBD and record distillate yield of 41% (clean product yield steady at 86%). Total processed inputs rose to 196.1 MMbbl (~2,131 MBD) from 186.9 MMbbl (~2,053 MBD) in 2Q, aided by lower turnaround spend ($79MM vs. $123MM).
- **Margin capture surged:** Realized refining margin jumped to $38.00/bbl from $24.08/bbl (+$13.92), driving refining adjusted pre-tax income to $6,060MM from $3,086MM — management attributes the gain to wider market crack spreads plus higher volumes/utilization, not just capture-rate improvement.
- **Renewable fuels margins compressed:** RFS segment pre-tax income fell to $191MM from $544MM on lower margins (including inventory impacts) and higher costs; renewable fuels production dipped to 47 MBD from 53 MBD — a soft read on RD/SAF economics this quarter.
- **Marketing margins also softened:** Marketing & Specialties adjusted pre-tax income dropped to $245MM from $514MM, explicitly tied to a "rising price environment" compressing global marketing fuel margins — a retail-side headwind even as refining crack spreads widened.
- **Capacity/logistics growth on track:** Coastal Bend expansion to begin initial volumes in 4Q26, ramping to 350 MBD by early 2027; Western Gateway Pipeline FID taken (in-service 2029); WRB full consolidation (100% Borger/Wood River since 10/1/25) delivering >$50MM in synergies.
- **Capital discipline intact:** $2.8B returned to shareholders (incl. $2.27B buybacks), debt cut $2.0B to $18.5B, net debt down $3.8B to $12.7B (net debt-to-cap 26%), and a second 2026 dividend hike signals confidence in sustaining payout despite segment mix shifts.

# HF Sinclair Q3 2026 – Refined Fuels Market Analysis

- **Crack spreads surged while throughput slipped**: Crude charge fell to 614,060 BPD (vs. 639,050 BPD in Q3 2025), with consolidated utilization down to 90.6% (from 94.3%), yet adjusted refinery gross margin more than tripled to **$54.22/bbl** (vs. $19.16/bbl, +183%) — reflecting a tight transportation-fuels market and widening crack spreads, not volume growth. Mid-Continent utilization dropped sharply to 96.3% (from 107.8%) due to the planned El Dorado turnaround, pulling Mid-Con sales mix lower while the West region offset with 87.0% utilization and stronger product demand.

- **RINs waivers are a material margin driver**: Management explicitly credits "small refinery RINs waivers granted by the EPA" alongside tight fuel supply as key contributors to the refining margin jump — signaling ongoing regulatory relief is flowing through to realized economics, not just market crack spreads.

- **Renewable diesel economics inflected positive**: Renewables segment swung to $123M segment income (from a $55M loss), with adjusted EBITDA of $109M (vs. -$13M) on improved RINs prices, higher Producer's Tax Credit (PTC) benefits, and volume growth to 63M gallons (from 57M). Adjusted renewables gross margin jumped to $2.11/gallon (from $0.18/gallon) — showing the PTC/RIN combination is now supportive rather than a drag.

- **Aggressive capital return underscores confidence**: $572M returned to shareholders in the quarter ($479M buybacks + $93M dividends), with cash building to $3,333M (from $978M at YE2025) against stable debt of $2,774M — signaling management views current margin strength as durable enough to fund both capex and heavy buybacks.

- **Structural portfolio shift underway**: Planned separation of the Lubricants & Specialties segment (≥80.1% distribution, targeted through 2027) plus the Mississauga, Ontario base oil refinery retirement (with $27M impairment, $28M severance, $54M accelerated D&A charges) signal HF Sinclair is narrowing its focus toward core refining/renewables/midstream, trimming lower-margin specialty exposure.

decks.title: 8-K exhibit dinoex99210-28x2026.htm (filed 2026-10-28)
decks.analysis:
## Key Takeaways

- **Leadership transition, not operational update:** This is a CEO/president succession announcement (Steve Ledbetter replacing Franklin Myers effective Jan 1, 2027); the filing contains no throughput, utilization, capture rate, or margin data for refined fuels or renewable diesel.

- **Lubricants & Specialties separation remains active:** Myers will stay on as executive chairperson post-transition specifically to advise on the "previously announced plan to pursue a separation" of the Lubricants & Specialties segment — signaling this portfolio restructuring is still a near-term strategic priority, not shelved.

- **Asset footprint confirmed:** HF Sinclair operates refineries in Kansas, Oklahoma, New Mexico, Wyoming, Washington, and Utah, and produces renewable diesel at two Wyoming facilities plus one New Mexico facility — no capacity figures or production volumes disclosed.

- **No RIN/LCFS or policy exposure commentary:** The release is silent on RIN pricing, LCFS credit values, 45Z or blender's credit exposure, or any renewable fuel economics guidance.

- **Capital allocation language is generic:** Incoming CEO Ledbetter cites "disciplined capital allocation" as a priority, but no specific capex, buyback, or dividend guidance changes are provided in this exhibit.

- **Marketing/distribution network reaffirmed:** Company reiterates supply to 1,850+ branded stations and 350+ Sinclair-licensed locations across the Southwest, Rocky Mountains, Pacific Northwest and Plains states, with lubricants exported to 80+ countries.

**What it signals:** This filing is purely a governance/leadership event with no new fundamental data for refined fuels markets, though the continued emphasis on the Lubricants & Specialties separation under new CEO oversight suggests investors should watch for a follow-on transaction announcement that could reshape HF Sinclair's capital structure and segment reporting in 2027.
